title.raw: 卷七十一 列傳第九: 斡魯 斡魯古勃堇 婆盧火 吾紮忽 闍母子:宗敘(本名德壽) Volume 71 Biographies 9: Wo Lu, Wolu Gubojin, Po Luhuo, Wu Zahu, She Mu and Son: Zongxu (Formerly Named Deshou)

sentences.zh: 列傳第九 ○斡魯 斡魯古勃堇 婆盧火 吾紮忽 闍母子 宗敘

translations.literal: Biography 9 ○ Wo Lu, Wolu gubojin, Po Luhuo, Wu Zahu, She Mu, Zongxu
translations.idiomatic: Biography 9. Wo Lu, Wolu gubojin, Po Luhuo, Wu Zahu, She Mu, and Zongxu

sentences.zh: (本名德壽)

translations.literal: (original name Deshou)
translations.idiomatic: (originally named Deshou)

sentences.zh: 斡魯，韓國公劾者第三子。

translations.literal: Wo Lu was the third son of Hezhe, Duke of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Lu was the third son of Hezhe, Duke of Han.

sentences.zh: 康宗初，蘇濱水含國部斡豁勃堇及斡准、聽備二部有異志，斡帶治之，斡賽、斡魯為之佐，遂伐斡豁，拔其城以歸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kang Zong's leadership, the Wohe lord of the Shuihan tribe in Sugobon and the Wohe and Tingbei tribal groups harbored hostile intent. Wo Dai punished them, with Wo Sai and Wo Lu assisting him; they then attacked Wohe, captured its city, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kang Zong's time, the Wohe lord of the Shuihan tribe at Sugobon and the Wohe and Tingbei groups showed disloyal intent. Wo Dai dealt with them, assisted by Wo Sai and Wo Lu; they attacked Wohe, took its city, and returned.

sentences.zh: 高麗築九城於曷懶甸。

translations.literal: Goryeo built nine cities in the Yalujiang region.
translations.idiomatic: Goryeo built nine fortified towns in the Yalujiang basin.

sentences.zh: 斡賽母疾病，斡魯代將其兵者數月。

translations.literal: Wo Sai's mother fell ill, and Wo Lu took command of her forces for several months.
translations.idiomatic: When Wo Sai's mother fell ill, Wo Lu commanded her troops in her stead for several months.

sentences.zh: 斡魯亦對築九城與高麗抗，出則戰，入則守，斡賽用之，卒城高麗。

translations.literal: Wo Lu also built nine cities opposite Goryeo's to resist them, fighting when they went out and defending when they withdrew; Wo Sai employed him, and in the end they walled Goryeo in.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Lu likewise built nine towns facing Goryeo's line and held them in check, fighting when the enemy came out and defending when they withdrew. Wo Sai relied on him, and in the end Goryeo was penned in behind its walls.

sentences.zh: 收國二年四月，詔斡魯統諸軍，與闍母、蒲察、迪古乃合咸州路都統斡魯古等，伐高永昌。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Shouguo, Wo Lu was ordered to command the various armies, and together with She Mu, Pucha, Digunai, and the Xianzhou Route commander-in-chief Wolugu and others, they attacked Gao Yongchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the second year of Shouguo, Wo Lu was ordered to take command of the armies. Together with She Mu, Pucha, Digunai, and the Xianzhou Route commander-in-chief Wolugu and others, he marched against Gao Yongchang.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「永昌誘脅戍卒，竊據一方，直投其隙而取之耳。

translations.literal: The edict said: "Yongchang has coerced garrison troops and seized a region for himself; we need only strike at his weakness to take him.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "Yongchang has coerced the garrison troops and seized a territory for himself. We need only strike where he is weak and take him.

sentences.zh: 此非有遠大計，其亡可立而待也。

translations.literal: This is not a man of far-reaching design; his fall may be expected at once.
translations.idiomatic: He has no far-reaching plan; his fall may be expected at once.

sentences.zh: 東京渤海人德我舊矣，易為招懷。

translations.literal: The Bohai people of the Eastern Capital have long known our virtue and may easily be won over.
translations.idiomatic: The Bohai of the Eastern Capital have long known our virtue and can easily be won over.

sentences.zh: 如其不從，即議進討，無事多殺。」

translations.literal: If they do not submit, then discuss advancing against them — there is no need to kill many."
translations.idiomatic: If they refuse, then plan an advance against them, but there is no need to slaughter many."

sentences.zh: 高永昌渤海人，在遼為裨將，以兵三千，屯東京八甔口。

translations.literal: Gao Yongchang was a Bohai man who had served in Liao as a deputy commander with three thousand troops stationed at the Eastern Capital's Badankou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yongchang was a Bohai who had served the Liao as a deputy commander. He held three thousand troops at Badankou near the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 永昌見遼政日敗，太祖起兵，遼人不能支，遂覬覦非常。

translations.literal: Seeing Liao's government daily decline and the Taizu raise his armies while the Liao could no longer hold them, Yongchang then set his sights on extraordinary power.
translations.idiomatic: Yongchang saw Liao's rule failing day by day, the Taizu raising his armies, and the Liao unable to resist; he then cast his eyes on extraordinary power.

sentences.zh: 是時，東京漢人與渤海人有怨，而多殺渤海人。

translations.literal: At that time the Han Chinese of the Eastern Capital and the Bohai were at odds, and many Bohai were killed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Han of the Eastern Capital bore a grudge against the Bohai, and many Bohai were killed.

sentences.zh: 永昌乃誘諸渤海，並其戍卒人據東京，旬月之間，遠近回應，有兵八千人，遂僭稱帝，改元隆基。

translations.literal: Yongchang therefore enticed the Bohai, joined his garrison troops, and seized the Eastern Capital; within a month distant and near responded, he had eight thousand troops, then usurped the imperial title and changed the era name to Longji.
translations.idiomatic: Yongchang then won over the Bohai, gathered the garrison troops, and seized the Eastern Capital. Within a month men near and far answered his call; he had eight thousand soldiers, usurped the imperial title, and declared the era name Longji.

sentences.zh: 遼人討之，久不能克。

translations.literal: The Liao attacked him but for a long time could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao campaigned against him but for a long time could not defeat him.

sentences.zh: 永昌使撻不野、杓合，以幣求救于太祖，且曰：「願並力以取遼。」

translations.literal: Yongchang sent Tabuye and Shaohe with gifts to beg aid from the Taizu, saying: "We wish to join forces to take Liao."
translations.idiomatic: Yongchang sent Tabuye and Shaohe with gifts to beg the Taizu for aid, saying, "Let us join forces to take Liao."

sentences.zh: 太祖使胡沙補往諭之曰：「同力取遼固可。

translations.literal: The Taizu sent Hu Shabu to instruct him, saying: "Joining forces to take Liao is certainly feasible.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu sent Hu Shabu to instruct him, saying, "Joining forces to take Liao is certainly possible.

sentences.zh: 東京近地，汝輒據之，以僭大號可乎。

translations.literal: The Eastern Capital lies close at hand, yet you seize it and presumptuously assume a grand title — is this permissible?
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Capital lies close at hand, yet you seize it and presumptuously take a grand title — how can that be allowed?

sentences.zh: 若能歸款，當處以王爵。

translations.literal: If you can return to allegiance, you will be granted a princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: If you return to allegiance, you will be granted a princely rank.

sentences.zh: 仍遣系遼籍女直胡突古來。」

translations.literal: He also sent Hutugu, a Jurchen registered under the Liao rolls, to come."
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Hutugu, a Jurchen registered on the Liao rolls, to go to him."

sentences.zh: 高永昌使撻不野與胡沙補、胡突古偕來，而永昌表辭不遜，且請還所俘渤海人。

translations.literal: Gao Yongchang had Tabuye come together with Hu Shabu and Hutugu, yet Yongchang's memorial language was disrespectful and he also requested the return of captured Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yongchang had Tabuye come with Hu Shabu and Hutugu, but Yongchang's memorial was disrespectful and he also demanded the return of captured Bohai.

sentences.zh: 太祖留胡突古不遣，遣大藥師奴與撻不野往招諭之。

translations.literal: The Taizu detained Hutugu and did not send him back, dispatching Dayaoshinu and Tabuye to summon and instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu kept Hutugu and did not send him back, dispatching Dayaoshinu and Tabuye to summon and instruct Yongchang.

sentences.zh: 斡魯方趨東京，遼兵六萬來攻照散城，阿徒罕勃堇、烏論石准與戰於益褪之地，大破之。

translations.literal: As Wo Lu was hurrying toward the Eastern Capital, sixty thousand Liao troops came to attack Zhaosan City; Atuhan lord and Ulun Shizhun fought them at Yitui and utterly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: As Wo Lu was pressing toward the Eastern Capital, sixty thousand Liao troops came to attack Zhaosan City. Atuhan lord and Ulun Shizhun met them at Yitui and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 五月，斡魯與遼軍遇於瀋州，敗之，進攻瀋州，取之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Wo Lu encountered the Liao army at Shenzhou, defeated them, advanced to attack Shenzhou, and took it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Wo Lu met the Liao army at Shenzhou, defeated it, pressed the attack on Shenzhou, and took the city.

sentences.zh: 永昌聞取瀋州，大懼，使家奴鐸刺以金印一、銀牌五十來，願去名號，稱籓。

translations.literal: Yongchang, hearing Shenzhou had been taken, was greatly afraid and sent his household slave Duoci with one gold seal and fifty silver tallies, wishing to abandon his title and become a tributary.
translations.idiomatic: When Yongchang heard Shenzhou had fallen, he was greatly afraid. He sent his household slave Duoci with one gold seal and fifty silver tallies, offering to abandon his title and submit as a vassal.

sentences.zh: 斡魯使胡沙補、撒八往報之。

translations.literal: Wo Lu sent Hu Shabu and Saba to report back to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Lu sent Hu Shabu and Saba to answer him.

sentences.zh: 會渤海高楨降，言永昌非真降者，特以緩師耳。

translations.literal: It happened that the Bohai Gao Zhen surrendered and said Yongchang was not truly submitting but only delaying the army.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Bohai Gao Zhen surrendered and said Yongchang was not truly submitting but only stalling the army.

sentences.zh: 斡魯進兵，永昌遂殺胡沙補等，率眾來拒。

translations.literal: Wo Lu advanced his troops, whereupon Yongchang killed Hu Shabu and the others and led his host to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Lu advanced. Yongchang then killed Hu Shabu and the others and led his forces out to resist.

sentences.zh: 遇於沃裏活水，我軍既濟，永昌之軍不戰而卻，逐北至東京城下。

translations.literal: They met at the Wolihuo River; once our army had crossed, Yongchang's troops gave battle without fighting and retreated; we pursued them north to below the walls of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: They met at the Wolihuo River. Once our army had crossed, Yongchang's troops withdrew without fighting. We pursued them north to the foot of the Eastern Capital walls.

sentences.zh: 明日，永昌盡率其眾來戰，複大敗之，遂以五千騎奔長松島。

translations.literal: The next day Yongchang led all his troops into battle and was again utterly defeated; he then fled with five thousand horsemen to Changsong Island.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Yongchang led all his troops into battle and was routed again. He fled with five thousand horsemen to Changsong Island.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖下甯江州，獲東京渤海人皆釋之，往往中道亡去，諸將請殺之，太祖曰：「既以克敵下城，何為多殺。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Taizu took Ningjiangzhou, all captured Eastern Capital Bohai were released, yet many fled away midway; the generals requested killing them, but the Taizu said: "Having already conquered the enemy and taken the city, why kill so many?
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Taizu took Ningjiangzhou, all captured Bohai of the Eastern Capital were released, yet many fled away along the road. The generals asked to kill them, but the Taizu said, "Having already defeated the enemy and taken the city, why slaughter so many?

sentences.zh: 昔先太師嘗破敵，獲百餘人，釋之，皆亡去。

translations.literal: In former days the late Grand Preceptor once defeated the enemy and captured more than a hundred men, released them, and all fled away.
translations.idiomatic: In former days the late Grand Preceptor once defeated the enemy, captured more than a hundred men, and released them; all fled away.

sentences.zh: 既而，往往招其部人來降。

translations.literal: Afterward they often recruited their tribesmen to come and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward they often brought their tribesmen in to surrender.

sentences.zh: 今此輩亡，後日當有效用者。」

translations.literal: Now that these people have fled, they will yet prove useful one day."
translations.idiomatic: Now that these men have fled, they will yet prove useful one day."

sentences.zh: 至是，東京人恩勝奴、仙哥等，執永昌妻子以城降，即甯江州所釋東京渤海人也。

translations.literal: At this time Enshengnu, Xiange, and others of the Eastern Capital seized Yongchang's wife and children and surrendered the city — they were the Eastern Capital Bohai released at Ningjiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At this point Enshengnu, Xiange, and others of the Eastern Capital seized Yongchang's wife and children and surrendered the city. They were the Eastern Capital Bohai released at Ningjiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 先太師，蓋謂世祖雲。

translations.literal: The late Grand Preceptor refers to the founding Ancestor Wanyan Yun.
translations.idiomatic: The late Grand Preceptor refers to the founding Ancestor Yun.

sentences.zh: 未幾，撻不野執永昌及鐸刺以獻，皆殺之。

translations.literal: Before long Tabuye seized Yongchang and Duoci and presented them; all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Tabuye seized Yongchang and Duoci and presented them; both were executed.

sentences.zh: 於是，遼之南路系籍女直及東京州縣盡降。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Liao's southern-route registered Jurchen and the Eastern Capital prefectures and counties all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Liao-registered Jurchen of the southern route and all the prefectures and counties of the Eastern Capital submitted.

sentences.zh: 以斡魯為南路都統、迭勃極烈，留烏蠢知東京事。

translations.literal: Wo Lu was made southern-route commander-in-chief and tier bojilie, leaving Wuchun to manage Eastern Capital affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Lu was appointed southern-route commander-in-chief and tier bojilie, with Wuchun left in charge of Eastern Capital affairs.

sentences.zh: 詔除遼法，省賦稅，置猛安謀克一如本朝之制。

translations.literal: An edict abolished Liao law, reduced taxes and levies, and established meng'an and company commands as in our own dynasty's system.
translations.idiomatic: An edict abolished Liao law, reduced taxes and levies, and established meng'an and company commands according to our own dynasty's system.

sentences.zh: 九月，斡魯上謁于婆魯買水，上慰勞之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Wo Lu came to audience at Baluimai River; the emperor comforted and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Wo Lu came to audience at Baluimai River, and the emperor comforted and praised him.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，幸斡魯第，張宴，官屬皆預，賜賚有差。

translations.literal: On xinhai the emperor visited Wo Lu's residence, spread a feast with all officials participating, and bestowed rewards in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai the emperor visited Wo Lu's residence, held a feast with all his officials in attendance, and bestowed rewards in varying measure.

sentences.zh: 燭偎水部實裏古達，殺酬斡、僕忽得，斡魯分胡刺古、烏蠢之兵討之。

translations.literal: Shiriguda of the Zhuweishui tribe killed Chouwo and Puhude; Wo Lu divided the troops of Hulagu and Wuchun to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Shiriguda of the Zhuweishui tribe killed Chouwo and Puhude. Wo Lu detached part of the forces of Hulagu and Wuchun to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 酬斡宗室子，魁偉善戰，年十五，隸軍中，多見任用。

translations.literal: Chouwo was a clansman, tall and skilled in battle; at fifteen he entered the army and was often employed.
translations.idiomatic: Chouwo was a clansman, tall and skilled in battle. At fifteen he entered the army and was often given command.

sentences.zh: 以兵五百，敗室韋，獲其民眾。

translations.literal: With five hundred troops he defeated the Shiwei and captured their people.
translations.idiomatic: With five hundred men he defeated the Shiwei and took their people captive.

sentences.zh: 及招降燭偎水部，以功為謀克。

translations.literal: When the Zhuweishui tribe was won over, he was made a company commander for his merit.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhuweishui tribe submitted, he was made a company commander for his merit.

sentences.zh: 僕忽得初事撒改，從討蕭海裏，降燭偎水部，領行軍千戶。

translations.literal: Puhude had first served Sagai, followed the campaign against Xiao Haili, reduced the Zhuweishui tribe, and led a field army thousand-household command.
translations.idiomatic: Puhude had first served Sagai, followed the campaign against Xiao Haili, subdued the Zhuweishui tribe, and held a field-army thousand-household command.

sentences.zh: 從破黃龍府，戰達魯古城，皆有功。

translations.literal: He followed in the capture of Huanglong Prefecture and fought at Dalu Ancient City, earning merit in both.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the capture of Huanglong Prefecture and fought at Dalu Ancient City, distinguishing himself in both.

sentences.zh: 其破甯江州，渤海乙塞補叛去，僕忽得追複之。

translations.literal: When Ningjiangzhou was taken, the Bohai Yisai Bu rebelled and fled; Puhude pursued and recovered him.
translations.idiomatic: When Ningjiangzhou fell, the Bohai Yisai Bu rebelled and fled; Puhude pursued and brought him back.

sentences.zh: 至是，與酬斡同被害。

translations.literal: At this time he was killed together with Chouwo.
translations.idiomatic: At this time he was killed together with Chouwo.

sentences.zh: 斡魯至石裏罕河，實裏古達遁去，追及於合撻刺山，誅其首惡四人，撫定餘眾。

translations.literal: Wo Lu reached the Shilihan River; Shiriguda fled, was overtaken at Hetaci Mountain, the four chief ringleaders were executed, and the remaining people were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Lu reached the Shilihan River. Shiriguda fled but was overtaken at Hetaci Mountain. The four chief ringleaders were executed and the rest of the people were pacified.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「汝討平叛亂，不勞師眾，朕甚嘉之。

translations.literal: The edict said: "You have suppressed the rebellion without troubling the army — I greatly commend this.
translations.idiomatic: The edict said, "You have put down the rebellion without troubling the army. I greatly commend this.

sentences.zh: 酬斡等死于國事，聞其屍棄於河，俟冰釋，必求以葬。

translations.literal: Chouwo and the others died in state service; hearing their bodies were cast into the river, when the ice melts they must be sought out for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Chouwo and the others died in the state's service. Hearing their bodies were cast into the river, when the ice melts you must recover them for burial.

sentences.zh: 其民可三百戶為一謀克，以眾所推服者領之，仍以其子弟等為質。」

translations.literal: Their people may be grouped three hundred households to a company command, led by one whom the multitude respects, and their sons and younger kin shall still be held as hostages."
translations.idiomatic: Their people may be organized into company commands of three hundred households each, led by men the people respect, with their sons and younger kin still held as hostages."

sentences.zh: 斡魯乃還。

translations.literal: Wo Lu then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Lu then returned.

sentences.zh: 天眷中，酬斡贈奉國上將軍，僕忽得贈昭義大將軍。

translations.literal: In the Tianjuan period Chouwo was posthumously granted General Who Upholds the State; Puhude was granted General of Manifest Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianjuan reign Chouwo was posthumously made General Who Upholds the State and Puhude General of Manifest Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 斡魯從都統襲遼主，遼主西走，西京已降複叛，敵據城西浮圖，下射攻城者。

translations.literal: Wo Lu followed the commander-in-chief in pursuing the Liao ruler; the Liao ruler fled west. The Western Capital had surrendered but rebelled again; the enemy held the pagoda west of the city and shot down at those attacking the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Lu followed the commander-in-chief in pursuing the Liao ruler, who fled west. The Western Capital had submitted but rebelled again. The enemy held the pagoda west of the city and shot down at the besiegers.

sentences.zh: 斡魯與鶻巴魯攻浮圖，奪之，複以精銳乘浮圖下射城中，遂破西京。

translations.literal: Wo Lu and Hubalu attacked the pagoda and seized it, then again with picked troops took the pagoda and shot down into the city, thereby taking the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Lu and Hubalu attacked the pagoda and took it. Then with picked troops they occupied the pagoda and shot down into the city, and so the Western Capital was taken.

sentences.zh: 夏國王使李良輔將兵三萬來救遼，次於天德之境。

translations.literal: The king of Xia sent Li Liangfu with thirty thousand troops to rescue Liao, encamping in the Tiande region.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Xia sent Li Liangfu with thirty thousand troops to rescue the Liao, encamping in the Tiande region.

sentences.zh: 婁室與斡魯合軍擊敗之，追至野穀，殺數千人。

translations.literal: Woshi and Wo Lu joined forces, defeated them, pursued to Yegu, and killed several thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Woshi and Wo Lu joined forces, defeated them, pursued to Yegu, and killed several thousand men.

sentences.zh: 夏人渡澗水，水暴至，漂溺者不可勝計。

translations.literal: The Xia men crossed the Jian River; the waters rose suddenly and those drowned could not be counted.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia forces crossed the Jian River. The waters rose suddenly and the drowned were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 遼主在陰山、青塚之間，斡魯為西南路都統，往襲之。

translations.literal: The Liao ruler was between Yinshan and Qingzhong; Wo Lu, as southwestern-route commander-in-chief, went to strike at him.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao ruler was between Yinshan and Qingzhong. Wo Lu, as southwestern-route commander-in-chief, went to strike at him.

sentences.zh: 使勃刺淑、撒曷懣以兵二百，襲遼權六院司喝離質於白水濼，獲之。

translations.literal: He sent Bolishu and Sahamen with two hundred troops to strike Helizhi, acting head of the Liao's Six Bureaus, at Baishu Marsh and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Bolishu and Sahamen with two hundred men to strike Helizhi, acting head of the Liao Six Bureaus, at Baishu Marsh and took him captive.

sentences.zh: 遼主留輜重於青塚，領兵一萬，往應州。

translations.literal: The Liao ruler left his baggage train at Qingzhong and led ten thousand troops toward Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao ruler left his baggage train at Qingzhong and led ten thousand troops toward Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 遣照裏、背答各率兵邀之，宗望奄至遼主營，盡俘其妻、子、宗族，得其傳國璽。

translations.literal: He dispatched Zhaoli and Beida each to lead troops and intercept him; Zongwang suddenly reached the Liao ruler's camp, captured all his wives, children, and clan, and obtained the dynastic seal.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhaoli and Beida each with troops to intercept him. Zongwang suddenly reached the Liao ruler's camp, captured his wives, children, and entire clan, and obtained the dynastic seal.

sentences.zh: 斡魯使使奏捷曰：「賴陛下威靈，屢敗敵兵，遼主無歸，勢必來降。

translations.literal: Wo Lu sent a messenger to report victory, saying: "Relying on Your Majesty's august power, we have repeatedly defeated the enemy. The Liao ruler has nowhere to return and will surely come to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Lu sent a messenger to report victory, saying, "By Your Majesty's august power we have repeatedly defeated the enemy. The Liao ruler has nowhere to return and will surely submit.

sentences.zh: 已嚴戒鄰境，毋納宋人，合饋軍糧，令銀術可往代州受之。」

translations.literal: The neighboring borders have been strictly warned not to admit Song men; grain for the army should be gathered and Yinjie sent to Daizhou to receive it."
translations.idiomatic: The neighboring borders have been strictly warned not to admit Song troops. Provisions for the army should be gathered and Yinjie sent to Daizhou to receive them."

sentences.zh: 詔：「遍諭有功將士，俟朕至彼，當次第推賞。

translations.literal: The edict said: "Announce throughout to meritorious officers and soldiers that when I arrive there, rewards will be granted in due order.
translations.idiomatic: The edict said, "Announce to all meritorious officers and soldiers that when I arrive there, rewards will be granted in due order.

sentences.zh: 遼主戚屬勿去其輿帳，善撫存之。

translations.literal: Do not remove the Liao ruler's kin from their carts and tents; treat them well and keep them safe.
translations.idiomatic: Do not remove the Liao ruler's kin from their carts and tents. Treat them well and keep them safe.

sentences.zh: 遼主伶俜去國，懷悲負恥，恐隕其命。

translations.literal: The Liao ruler, alone and exiled from his state, bears grief and shame and may fear for his life.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao ruler, alone and exiled from his state, bears grief and shame and may fear for his life.

sentences.zh: 孽雖自作，而嘗居大位，深所不忍。

translations.literal: Though his crime was of his own making, he once held the great position — this is deeply hard to bear.
translations.idiomatic: Though his crime was of his own making, he once held the throne, and that is deeply hard to bear.

sentences.zh: 如招之肯來，以其宗族付之。

translations.literal: If he can be summoned and is willing to come, entrust his clan to him.
translations.idiomatic: If he can be summoned and is willing to come, entrust his clan to him.

sentences.zh: 已遣楊璞征糧于宋，銀術可不須往矣。

translations.literal: Yang Pu has already been sent to levy grain from the Song; Yinjie need not go.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Pu has already been sent to levy grain from the Song; Yinjie need not go.

sentences.zh: 遼趙王習泥烈及諸官吏，並釋其罪，且撫慰之。」

translations.literal: The Liao Prince of Zhao Xinilie and all officials are likewise pardoned of their crimes and comforted."
translations.idiomatic: The Liao Prince of Zhao Xinilie and all officials are likewise pardoned and comforted."

sentences.zh: 太祖還京師，宗翰為西北、西南兩路都統，斡魯及蒲家奴副之。

translations.literal: When the Taizu returned to the capital, Zonghan was made commander-in-chief of the northwest and southwest routes, with Wo Lu and Pujianu as his deputies.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taizu returned to the capital, Zonghan was made commander-in-chief of the northwest and southwest routes, with Wo Lu and Pujianu as his deputies.

sentences.zh: 宗翰朝京師，詔：「以夏人言，宋侵略新割地，以便宜決之。」

translations.literal: When Zonghan came to court at the capital, an edict said: "According to the Xia people, the Song are encroaching on the newly ceded lands — decide the matter as circumstances require."
translations.idiomatic: When Zonghan came to court at the capital, an edict said, "According to the Xia, the Song are encroaching on the newly ceded lands. Decide the matter as circumstances require."

sentences.zh: 斡魯奏曰：「夏人不盡歸戶口資帑，又以宋人侵賜地求援兵。

translations.literal: Wo Lu memorialized, saying: "The Xia have not fully returned the households and stored goods, and they also seek relief troops because Song men are encroaching on the lands granted them.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Lu memorialized, saying, "The Xia have not fully returned the households and stored goods, and they also seek relief troops because Song men are encroaching on the lands granted them.

sentences.zh: 宋之邊臣將取所賜夏人疆土，蓋有異圖。」

translations.literal: Song border officials intend to take the territory granted the Xia — they surely have ulterior designs."
translations.idiomatic: Song border officials intend to take the territory granted the Xia. They surely have ulterior designs."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「夏人屢求援兵者，或不欲歸我戶口，沮吾追襲遼主事也。

translations.literal: The edict said: "Those Xia who repeatedly seek relief troops may not wish to return our households and are obstructing our pursuit of the Liao ruler.
translations.idiomatic: The edict said, "Those Xia who repeatedly seek relief troops may not wish to return our households and are obstructing our pursuit of the Liao ruler.

sentences.zh: 宋人敢言自取疆土于夏，誠有異圖。

translations.literal: The Song dare speak of taking territory from the Xia themselves — they truly have ulterior designs.
translations.idiomatic: The Song dare speak of taking territory from the Xia themselves — they truly have ulterior designs.

sentences.zh: 宜謹守備，盡索在夏戶口，通聞兩國，事審處之。」

translations.literal: You should strictly maintain defenses, demand all households still in Xia territory, inform both states, and settle the matter after careful review."
translations.idiomatic: Strictly maintain your defenses, demand all households still in Xia territory, inform both states, and settle the matter after careful review."

sentences.zh: 斡魯複請弗割山西與宋，則遼主不能與宋郭藥師交通。

translations.literal: Wo Lu again requested that Shanxi not be ceded to the Song, so the Liao ruler could not communicate with the Song's Guo Yaoshi.
translations.idiomatic: Wo Lu again requested that Shanxi not be ceded to the Song, so the Liao ruler could not communicate with the Song's Guo Yaoshi.

sentences.zh: 複詔曰：「宗翰請毋與宋山西地，卿複及此，疆場之事當慎毋忽。」

translations.literal: Another edict said: "Zonghan asks that Shanxi not be given to the Song, and you again raise this — border affairs must be handled with care and not neglected."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said, "Zonghan asks that Shanxi not be given to the Song, and you again raise this. Border affairs must be handled with care and not neglected."

sentences.zh: 及宗翰等伐宋，斡魯行西南、西北兩路都統事。

translations.literal: When Zonghan and the others campaigned against the Song, Wo Lu administered the affairs of commander-in-chief of the southwest and northwest routes.
translations.idiomatic: When Zonghan and the others campaigned against the Song, Wo Lu administered the affairs of commander-in-chief of the southwest and northwest routes.

sentences.zh: 天會五年，薨。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianhui he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianhui he died.

sentences.zh: 皇統五年，追封鄭國王。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Huangtong he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Huangtong he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 天德二年，酏享太祖廟廷。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiande he received posthumous libation in the Taizu temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiande he received posthumous libation in the Taizu temple hall.

sentences.zh: 子撒八，銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His son Saba was made Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: His son Saba was made Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 子賽裏。

translations.literal: His son Saili.
translations.idiomatic: His son Saili.

sentences.zh: 斡魯古勃堇

translations.literal: Wolu gubojin
translations.idiomatic: Wolu gubojin

sentences.zh: 斡魯古勃堇，宗室子也。

translations.literal: Wolu gubojin was a clansman.
translations.idiomatic: Wolu gubojin was a member of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 太祖伐遼，使斡魯古、阿魯撫諭斡忽、急賽兩路系遼女直，與遼節度使撻不也戰，敗之，斬撻不也，酷輦嶺阿魯台罕等十四太彎皆降，斡忽、急賽兩路亦降。

translations.literal: When the Taizu attacked Liao, he sent Wolugu and Aru to win over the Wohu and Jisai routes of Liao-registered Jurchen; they fought the Liao military commissioner Tabuye, defeated him, beheaded Tabuye, and the fourteen great chiefs including Arutaihan of Kulian Ridge all surrendered; the Wohu and Jisai routes also submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taizu attacked the Liao, he sent Wolugu and Aru to win over the Wohu and Jisai routes of Liao-registered Jurchen. They fought the Liao military commissioner Tabuye, defeated him, and beheaded him. The fourteen great chiefs including Arutaihan of Kulian Ridge all submitted, and the Wohu and Jisai routes followed.

sentences.zh: 與遼都統實婁戰於鹹州西，敗之，斬實婁於陣，與婁室克鹹州。

translations.literal: He fought the Liao commander-in-chief Shilou west of Xianzhou, defeated him, beheaded Shilou on the field, and with Woshi took Xianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He fought the Liao commander-in-chief Shilou west of Xianzhou, defeated him, and beheaded Shilou on the battlefield. Together with Woshi he took Xianzhou.

sentences.zh: 陁滿忽吐以所部降于斡魯古，鄰部戶七千亦來歸，遂與遼將喝補戰，破其軍數萬人。

translations.literal: Tuomanhutu submitted with his command to Wolugu; seven thousand households of neighboring tribes also came over; he then fought the Liao general Hebu and broke an army of tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Tuomanhutu submitted with his command to Wolugu, and seven thousand households of neighboring tribes also came over. He then fought the Liao general Hebu and routed an army of tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉之，以為咸州軍帥。

translations.literal: The Taizu commended him and made him military commander of Xianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu praised him and appointed him military commander of Xianzhou.

sentences.zh: 斡魯伐高永昌于東京，斡魯古以鹹州軍佐之。

translations.literal: When Wo Lu attacked Gao Yongchang at the Eastern Capital, Wolugu assisted him with the Xianzhou army.
translations.idiomatic: When Wo Lu attacked Gao Yongchang at the Eastern Capital, Wolugu assisted with the Xianzhou army.

sentences.zh: 遼秦晉國王耶律捏裏來伐，迪古乃、婁室、婆盧火等將二萬眾，合斡魯古鹹州兵往擊之。

translations.literal: The Liao Prince of Qin and Jin, Yelü Nieli, came to attack; Digunai, Woshi, Po Luhuo, and others led twenty thousand men, joining Wolugu's Xianzhou troops to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao Prince of Qin and Jin, Yelü Nieli, came to attack. Digunai, Woshi, Po Luhuo, and others led twenty thousand men and, joining Wolugu's Xianzhou troops, went to strike him.

sentences.zh: 胡突古嘗叛入於遼，居於東京，高永昌據東京，太祖索之以歸。

translations.literal: Hutugu had once defected to the Liao and lived at the Eastern Capital; when Gao Yongchang seized the Eastern Capital, the Taizu demanded his return.
translations.idiomatic: Hutugu had once defected to the Liao and lived at the Eastern Capital. When Gao Yongchang seized the Eastern Capital, the Taizu demanded his return.

sentences.zh: 斡魯古伐永昌，以便宜署胡突古為千戶。

translations.literal: When Wolugu attacked Yongchang, he provisionally appointed Hutugu as a thousand-household commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Wolugu attacked Yongchang, he provisionally appointed Hutugu as a thousand-household commander.

sentences.zh: 散都魯、訛魯補皆無功，亦以便宜除官。

translations.literal: Sandulu and Elubu had both achieved nothing, yet were likewise given provisional appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Sandulu and Elubu had both achieved nothing, yet were likewise given provisional appointments.

sentences.zh: 及以便宜解權謀克斛拔魯、黃哥、達及保等職，皆非其罪。

translations.literal: He also provisionally removed from office the acting company commanders Hubalu, Huangge, Daji, Bao, and others — none of whom were guilty.
translations.idiomatic: He also provisionally removed the acting company commanders Hubalu, Huangge, Daji, Bao, and others from office, though none were guilty.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞之，盡複斛拔魯等謀克，胡突古等皆罷去。

translations.literal: When the Taizu heard of this, he restored Hubalu and the other company commands; Hutugu and the others were all dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taizu heard of this, he restored Hubalu and the others to their company commands. Hutugu and the rest were all dismissed.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞斡魯古軍中往往闕馬，而官馬多匿於私家，遂檢括之。

translations.literal: The Taizu heard that in Wolugu's army horses were often lacking while government horses were largely hidden in private households, and so ordered a roundup.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu heard that Wolugu's army often lacked horses while government horses were largely hidden in private households, and ordered a roundup.

sentences.zh: 耶律捏裏、佛頂遺斡魯古書，請和。

translations.literal: Yelü Nieli and Fotou sent Wolugu letters requesting peace.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Nieli and Fotou sent Wolugu letters requesting peace.

sentences.zh: 斡魯古以捏裏書並所答書來上，且請曰：「複有書問，宜如何報之？」

translations.literal: Wolugu sent up Nieli's letter together with his reply and also requested: "If there are further letters, how should they be answered?"
translations.idiomatic: Wolugu sent up Nieli's letter together with his reply and asked, "If further letters come, how should they be answered?"

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「若彼再來請和，汝當以阿疏等叛亡，索而不獲至於交兵，我行人賽刺亦不遣還。

translations.literal: The edict said: "If they again come requesting peace, you should cite Ashu and others who rebelled and fled, whom we demanded but did not recover, leading to battle; our envoy Saici we likewise will not send back.
translations.idiomatic: The edict said, "If they again request peace, you should cite Ashu and others who rebelled and fled, whom we demanded but did not recover, leading to battle. Our envoy Saici we likewise will not send back.

sentences.zh: 若歸賽刺，及送阿疏等，則和好之議方敢奏聞。

translations.literal: If Saici is returned and Ashu and the others are handed over, then the proposal of peace may be reported.
translations.idiomatic: Only if Saici is returned and Ashu and the others are handed over may a proposal of peace be reported.

sentences.zh: 仍恐議和非實，無失備禦。」

translations.literal: Still fearing the peace talks may not be genuine, do not neglect defenses."
translations.idiomatic: Still fearing the peace talks may not be genuine, do not neglect your defenses."

sentences.zh: 耶律捏裏軍蒺藜山，斡魯古以兵一萬，戍東京。

translations.literal: Yelü Nieli's army was at Jili Mountain; Wolugu garrisoned the Eastern Capital with ten thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Nieli's army was at Jili Mountain. Wolugu garrisoned the Eastern Capital with ten thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 太祖使迪古乃、婁室複以兵一萬益之，詔曰：「遼主失道，肆命徂征，惟爾將士，當體朕意，拒命者討之，服者撫安之。

translations.literal: The Taizu sent Digunai and Woshi with another ten thousand troops to reinforce them. The edict said: "The Liao ruler has lost the Way and I have been charged to campaign against him. You officers and soldiers must embody my intent: those who resist are to be punished, those who submit are to be pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu sent Digunai and Woshi with another ten thousand troops as reinforcements. The edict said, "The Liao ruler has lost the Way and I have been charged to campaign against him. You officers and soldiers must embody my intent: punish those who resist and pacify those who submit.

sentences.zh: 毋貪俘掠，毋肆殺戮。

translations.literal: Do not greedily seize captives and booty; do not slaughter wantonly.
translations.idiomatic: Do not greedily seize captives and booty, and do not slaughter wantonly.

sentences.zh: 所賜捏裏詔書，可傳致也。」

translations.literal: The edict granted to Nieli may be transmitted to him."
translations.idiomatic: The edict granted to Nieli may be delivered to him."

sentences.zh: 詔捏裏曰：「汝等誠欲請和，當廢黜昏主，擇立賢者，副朕吊伐之意，然後可議和約。

translations.literal: The edict to Nieli said: "If you truly wish to seek peace, you must depose the benighted ruler and choose a worthy man to install, in accord with my intent to succor the afflicted and punish the wicked; only then may a treaty be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: The edict to Nieli said, "If you truly wish peace, depose your benighted ruler and choose a worthy man to install, in keeping with my intent to succor the afflicted and punish the wicked. Only then may we discuss a treaty.

sentences.zh: 不然，當盡並爾國。

translations.literal: Otherwise your state shall be wholly annexed.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise your state shall be wholly annexed.

sentences.zh: 其審圖之。」

translations.literal: Consider this carefully."
translations.idiomatic: Consider this carefully."

sentences.zh: 捏裏複書斡魯古，雲：「降去人痕孛見還，則當送阿疏等。」

translations.literal: Nieli again wrote to Wolugu, saying: "If the surrendered men Henbo and others are returned, then Ashu and the others will be sent."
translations.idiomatic: Nieli wrote again to Wolugu, saying, "If the surrendered men Henbo and others are returned, then Ashu and the others will be sent."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「痕孛等乃交兵之後來降，阿疏則平日以罪亡去，其事特異。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Henbo and the others surrendered after battle had been joined; Ashu fled in ordinary times because of a crime — the cases are quite different."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Henbo and the others surrendered after fighting had begun; Ashu fled in ordinary times because of a crime. The cases are quite different."

sentences.zh: 複詔捏裏，令此月十三日送阿疏至顯州，各遣重臣議疆場事。

translations.literal: He again instructed Nieli to have Ashu delivered to Xianzhou on the thirteenth of this month, and each side was to send high ministers to discuss border affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He again instructed Nieli to deliver Ashu to Xianzhou on the thirteenth of this month, and each side was to send senior ministers to discuss border affairs.

sentences.zh: 斡魯古等攻顯州，知東京事完顏斡論以兵來會，即以兵三千先渡遼水，得降戶千余，遂薄顯州。

translations.literal: Wolugu and the others attacked Xianzhou. Wanyan Wolun, who managed Eastern Capital affairs, came with troops to join them; he first crossed the Liao River with three thousand men, gained more than a thousand surrendered households, and then pressed close to Xianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wolugu and the others attacked Xianzhou. Wanyan Wolun, who managed Eastern Capital affairs, came with troops to join them. He first crossed the Liao River with three thousand men, gained more than a thousand surrendered households, and pressed close to Xianzhou.

sentences.zh: 郭藥師乘夜來襲，斡論擊走之。

translations.literal: Guo Yaoshi came by night to raid them; Wolun struck and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yaoshi raided them by night; Wolun struck and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 斡魯古等遂與捏裏等戰於蒺藜山，大敗遼兵，追北至阿裏真陂，獲佛頂家屬。

translations.literal: Wolugu and the others then fought Nieli and the others at Jili Mountain, utterly defeated the Liao army, pursued north to Alizhen Marsh, and captured Fotou's family.
translations.idiomatic: Wolugu and the others then fought Nieli and his forces at Jili Mountain, routed the Liao army, pursued north to Alizhen Marsh, and captured Fotou's family.

sentences.zh: 遂圍顯州，攻其城西南，軍士神篤逾城先入，燒其佛寺，煙焰撲人，守陴者不能立，諸軍乘之，遂拔顯州。

translations.literal: They then besieged Xianzhou, attacking the southwest of the city. The soldier Shendu scaled the wall first, burned the Buddhist temple, and the smoke and flames assailed the men; those defending the parapets could not stand, the armies pressed the advantage, and Xianzhou was taken.
translations.idiomatic: They then besieged Xianzhou, attacking from the southwest. The soldier Shendu scaled the wall first and burned the Buddhist temple. Smoke and flames assailed the defenders, who could not hold the parapets. The armies pressed the advantage and took Xianzhou.

sentences.zh: 於是、乾、懿、豪、徽、成、川、惠等州皆降。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yu, Gan, Yi, Hao, Hui, Cheng, Chuan, and Hui prefectures all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Yu, Gan, Yi, Hao, Hui, Cheng, Chuan, and Hui prefectures all submitted.

sentences.zh: 乾州後為閭陽縣，遼諸陵多在此，禁無所犯。

translations.literal: Gan Prefecture later became Luyang County; many Liao imperial tombs were there, and nothing was permitted to violate them.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Prefecture later became Luyang County. Many Liao imperial tombs lay there, and nothing was permitted to violate them.

sentences.zh: 徙成、川州人於同、銀二州居之。

translations.literal: The people of Cheng and Chuan prefectures were moved to dwell in Tong and Yin prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Cheng and Chuan prefectures were relocated to Tong and Yin prefectures.

sentences.zh: 捏裏再以書來請和，斡魯古承前詔，以阿疏為言，答之。

translations.literal: Nieli again sent a letter requesting peace; Wolugu, following the earlier edict, answered citing Ashu.
translations.idiomatic: Nieli again sent a letter requesting peace. Wolugu, following the earlier edict, answered citing Ashu.

sentences.zh: 駐軍顯州以聽命。

translations.literal: The army encamped at Xianzhou awaiting orders.
translations.idiomatic: The army encamped at Xianzhou to await orders.

sentences.zh: 賜斡魯古等馬十匹，詔曰：「汝等力摧大敵，攻下諸城，朕甚嘉之。

translations.literal: Ten horses were granted to Wolugu and the others. The edict said: "You have forcefully shattered a great enemy and taken many cities — I greatly commend this.
translations.idiomatic: Ten horses were granted to Wolugu and the others. The edict said, "You have shattered a great enemy and taken many cities. I greatly commend this.

sentences.zh: 遼主未獲，人心易搖，不可恃戰勝而失備禦。」

translations.literal: The Liao ruler has not yet been captured; hearts are easily shaken; you must not rely on victory and neglect defenses."
translations.idiomatic: The Liao ruler has not yet been captured, and hearts are easily shaken. You must not rely on victory and neglect your defenses."

sentences.zh: 遼雙州節度使張崇降，斡魯古以便宜命複其職，仍令世襲。

translations.literal: Zhang Chong, military commissioner of Liao's Shuangzhou, surrendered; Wolugu provisionally restored him to office and still ordered the post to pass by inheritance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chong, military commissioner of Liao's Shuangzhou, surrendered. Wolugu provisionally restored him to office and ordered the post to remain hereditary.

sentences.zh: 斡魯古久在鹹州，多立功，亦多自恣，劾裏保、雙古等告斡魯古不法事：遼帝在中京可追襲而不追襲，鹹州糧草豐足而奏數不以實，攻顯州獲生口財畜多自取。

translations.literal: Wolugu had long been at Xianzhou, achieving many merits but also often acting willfully. Helibao, Shuanggu, and others reported Wolugu's unlawful acts: the Liao emperor was at Central Capital and could have been pursued but was not; Xianzhou had abundant grain and fodder yet the reports did not reflect the true numbers; when Xianzhou was attacked the captives and livestock taken were largely kept for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Wolugu had long been at Xianzhou, achieving many merits but also often acting willfully. Helibao, Shuanggu, and others reported Wolugu's unlawful conduct: the Liao emperor was at Central Capital and could have been pursued but was not; Xianzhou had abundant grain and fodder yet his reports did not reflect the true amounts; when Xianzhou was taken, many captives and livestock were kept for himself.

sentences.zh: 捏裏、孛刺束等亦告孛堇瞢葛、麻吉、窩論、赤閏、阿刺本、乙刺等多取生口財畜。

translations.literal: Nieli, Boleshu, and others also reported that the lords Mengge, Maji, Wolun, Chihun, Aciben, Yici, and others had taken many captives and livestock.
translations.idiomatic: Nieli, Boleshu, and others also reported that the lords Mengge, Maji, Wolun, Chihun, Aciben, Yici, and others had taken many captives and livestock.

sentences.zh: 遂以闍哥代為咸州路都銑。

translations.literal: Zhege was therefore made Xianzhou Route commander-in-chief in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Zhege was therefore made Xianzhou Route commander-in-chief in his place.

sentences.zh: 闍哥亦宗室子也，既代斡魯古治鹹州。

translations.literal: Zhege was also a clansman; having replaced Wolugu in governing Xianzhou,
translations.idiomatic: Zhege was also a clansman. Having replaced Wolugu in governing Xianzhou,

sentences.zh: 初，迪古乃、婁室奏，攻顯州新降附之民，可遷其富者于咸州路，其貧者徙內地。

translations.literal: earlier Digunai and Woshi had memorialized that among the newly submitted people after the capture of Xianzhou, the wealthy might be moved to the Xianzhou Route and the poor relocated inland.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Digunai and Woshi had memorialized that among the people newly submitted after the capture of Xianzhou, the wealthy might be moved to the Xianzhou Route and the poor relocated inland.

sentences.zh: 於是，詔使闍哥擇其才可幹事者授之謀克，其豪右誠心歸附者擬為猛安，錄其姓名以聞，饑貧之民，官賑給之，而使闍母為其副統雲。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered Zhege to choose those capable of service and appoint them as company commanders; among the powerful who sincerely submitted, meng'an posts were to be proposed, their names recorded and reported, hungry and poor people were to be given relief by the state, and She Mu was made deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon an edict ordered Zhege to choose those capable of service and appoint them as company commanders. Among the powerful who sincerely submitted, meng'an posts were to be proposed, their names recorded and reported, the hungry and poor were to receive state relief, and She Mu was made deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 久之，遼通、祺、雙、遼四州之民八百餘家，詣鹹州都統降。

translations.literal: After a long time, more than eight hundred households of the people of Liao's Tong, Qi, Shuang, and Liao prefectures came to surrender to the Xianzhou commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time, more than eight hundred households from Liao's Tong, Qi, Shuang, and Liao prefectures came to surrender to the Xianzhou commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「遼人賦斂無度，民不堪命，相率求生，不可使失望，分置諸部，擇善地以處之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The Liao levy taxes without limit and the people cannot bear it; they have banded together to seek life. They must not be disappointed — distribute them among the tribes and settle them in good lands."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The Liao levy taxes without limit and the people cannot bear it. They have banded together to seek a living. They must not be disappointed. Distribute them among the tribes and settle them in good lands."

sentences.zh: 太祖召斡魯古自問之，斡魯古引伏。

translations.literal: The Taizu summoned Wolugu to question him personally; Wolugu confessed.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu summoned Wolugu to question him in person; Wolugu confessed.

sentences.zh: 闍哥鞫窩論等。

translations.literal: Zhege tried Wolun and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Zhege tried Wolun and the others.

sentences.zh: 詔降斡魯古為謀克，而禁錮窩論等。

translations.literal: An edict demoted Wolugu to company commander and imprisoned Wolun and the others.
translations.idiomatic: An edict demoted Wolugu to company commander and imprisoned Wolun and the others.

sentences.zh: 天輔六年，討賊于牛心山，道病卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianfu he campaigned against bandits at Niuxin Mountain and died of illness on the road.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianfu he campaigned against bandits at Niuxin Mountain and died of illness on the march.

sentences.zh: 天眷中，贈特進。

translations.literal: During the Tianjuan reign he was posthumously granted Special Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianjuan reign he was posthumously granted Special Advancement.

sentences.zh: 天德二年，配享太祖廟廷。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiande he was given a place in the Taizu temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiande he was given a place in the Taizu temple hall.

sentences.zh: 大定十五年，諡莊翼。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Dading he was given the posthumous title Zhuangyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Dading he was given the posthumous title Zhuangyi.

sentences.zh: 婆盧火

translations.literal: Po Luhuo
translations.idiomatic: Po Luhuo

sentences.zh: 婆盧火，安帝五代孫。

translations.literal: Po Luhuo was a fifth-generation descendant of Emperor An.
translations.idiomatic: Po Luhuo was a fifth-generation descendant of Emperor An.

sentences.zh: 太祖伐遼，使婆盧火征迪古乃兵，失期，杖之。

translations.literal: When the Taizu attacked Liao, he sent Po Luhuo to levy Digunai's troops; he missed the deadline and was flogged.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taizu attacked the Liao, he sent Po Luhuo to levy Digunai's troops. He missed the deadline and was flogged.

sentences.zh: 後與渾黜以四千人，往助婁室、銀術哥攻黃龍府。

translations.literal: Later, with Hunchu and four thousand men, he went to assist Woshi and Yinshuge in attacking Huanglong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later, with Hunchu and four thousand men, he went to assist Woshi and Yinshuge in attacking Huanglong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 辭勒罕、撒孛得兄弟，直攧裏部人，嘗寇耶懶路，穆宗遣婆盧火討之。

translations.literal: Cilehan and the brothers Sabede, men of the Zhizhanli tribe, had once raided the Yalujiang route; Muzong sent Po Luhuo to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Cilehan and the brothers Sabede, men of the Zhizhanli tribe, had once raided the Yalujiang route. Muzong sent Po Luhuo to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 至阿裏門河，辭勒罕偽降，遂略馬畜三百而去，複掠兀勒部二十五寨。

translations.literal: At the Alimen River, Cilehan feigned surrender, then plundered three hundred horses and livestock and departed, and again raided twenty-five stockades of the Wule tribe.
translations.idiomatic: At the Alimen River, Cilehan feigned surrender, then plundered three hundred horses and livestock and departed, and again raided twenty-five stockades of the Wule tribe.

sentences.zh: 太祖複使婆盧火討之。

translations.literal: The Taizu again sent Po Luhuo to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu again sent Po Luhuo to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 婆盧火渡蘇袞河，招降旁近諸部，因籍丁壯為軍，至特滕吳水，轍孛得偽降，複叛去，執而殺之。

translations.literal: Po Luhuo crossed the Suchun River, won over nearby tribes, enrolled able-bodied men as soldiers, and at the Tetengwu River Zhebede feigned surrender and rebelled again; he was seized and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Po Luhuo crossed the Suchun River, won over nearby tribes, and enrolled able-bodied men as soldiers. At the Tetengwu River, Zhebede feigned surrender and rebelled again; he was seized and executed.

sentences.zh: 婆盧火至特鄰城，圍之，辭勒罕遁去。

translations.literal: Po Luhuo reached Telin City, besieged it, and Cilehan fled.
translations.idiomatic: Po Luhuo reached Telin City and besieged it; Cilehan fled.

sentences.zh: 婆盧火破其城，執其妻子，辭勒罕遂降，曰：「我之馬牛財貨盡矣，何以為生。」

translations.literal: Po Luhuo stormed the city, seized his wife and children, and Cilehan then submitted, saying: "My horses, cattle, and goods are all gone — how am I to live?"
translations.idiomatic: Po Luhuo stormed the city and seized his wife and children. Cilehan then submitted, saying, "My horses, cattle, and goods are all gone. How am I to live?"

sentences.zh: 婆盧火與之馬十匹。

translations.literal: Po Luhuo gave him ten horses.
translations.idiomatic: Po Luhuo gave him ten horses.

sentences.zh: 直攧裏部產良馬，太祖使紇石烈阿習罕掌其畜牧，婆盧火及子婆速，俱為謀克。

translations.literal: The Zhizhanli tribe produced fine horses; the Taizu had the Heshilie Axihan oversee their herding; Po Luhuo and his son Basu were both made company commanders.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhizhanli tribe produced fine horses. The Taizu had the Heshilie Axihan oversee their herding. Po Luhuo and his son Basu were both made company commanders.

sentences.zh: 天輔五年，摘取諸路猛安中萬餘家，屯田於泰州，婆盧火為都統，賜耕牛五十。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianfu, more than ten thousand households were taken from meng'an across the routes and settled for garrison farming at Taizhou; Po Luhuo was made commander-in-chief and granted fifty plow oxen.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianfu, more than ten thousand households were taken from meng'an across the routes and settled for garrison farming at Taizhou. Po Luhuo was made commander-in-chief and granted fifty plow oxen.

sentences.zh: 婆盧火舊居按出虎水，自是徙居泰州，而遣拾得、查端、阿裏徒歡、奚撻罕等俱徙焉。

translations.literal: Po Luhuo had formerly lived on the Anchuhu River; from this time he moved to Taizhou, and Shide, Chaduan, Alituhuan, Xi Tahan, and others were all relocated with him.
translations.idiomatic: Po Luhuo had formerly lived on the Anchuhu River. From this time he moved to Taizhou, and Shide, Chaduan, Alituhuan, Xi Tahan, and others were all relocated with him.

sentences.zh: 唯族子撒刺喝嘗為世祖養子，獨得不徙。

translations.literal: Only his clansman Sacihe, who had once been adopted by the founding Ancestor, alone was not moved.
translations.idiomatic: Only his clansman Sacihe, who had once been adopted by the founding Ancestor, was not relocated.

sentences.zh: 太祖取燕京，婆盧火為右翼，兵出居庸關，大敗遼兵，遂取居庸。

translations.literal: When the Taizu took Yanjing, Po Luhuo was on the right wing; the army went out through Juyong Pass, utterly defeated the Liao army, and then took Juyong.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taizu took Yanjing, Po Luhuo served on the right wing. The army went out through Juyong Pass, routed the Liao army, and took Juyong.

sentences.zh: 蕭妃遁去，都監高六等來送款乞降。

translations.literal: Consort Xiao fled; Director-in-chief Gao Liu and others came to offer allegiance and beg to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Xiao fled. Director-in-chief Gao Liu and others came to offer allegiance and beg to surrender.

sentences.zh: 習古乃追蕭妃至古北口，蕭妃已過三日，不及而還。

translations.literal: Xigunai pursued Consort Xiao to Gubeikou; she had already passed three days before and he returned without overtaking her.
translations.idiomatic: Xigunai pursued Consort Xiao to Gubeikou, but she had already passed three days before and he returned without overtaking her.

sentences.zh: 上令婆盧火、胡實賚率輕騎追之，蕭妃已遠去，獲其從官統軍察刺、宣徽查刺，並其家族，及銀牌二、印十有一。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Po Luhuo and Hu Shilai to lead light cavalry in pursuit; Consort Xiao was already far away, but they captured her attendant officials, army commander Chaci and palace commissioner Chaci, together with their families, as well as two silver tallies and eleven seals.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Po Luhuo and Hu Shilai to lead light cavalry in pursuit. Consort Xiao was already far away, but they captured her attendant officials, army commander Chaci and palace commissioner Chaci, together with their families, as well as two silver tallies and eleven seals.

sentences.zh: 及迭刺叛，婆盧火、石古乃討平之，其群官率眾降者，就使領其所部。

translations.literal: When Dieci rebelled, Po Luhuo and Shigunai suppressed and pacified them; officials who led their followers in surrender were left to command their own commands.
translations.idiomatic: When Dieci rebelled, Po Luhuo and Shigunai suppressed and pacified them. Officials who led their followers in surrender were left to command their own units.

sentences.zh: 太宗以空名宣頭及銀牌給之。

translations.literal: The Taizong gave them blank edict headers and silver tallies.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizong gave them blank edict headers and silver tallies.

sentences.zh: 同時有婆盧火者，婁室平陝西，婆盧火、繩果監戰。

translations.literal: At the same time there was another Po Luhuo: when Woshi pacified Shaanxi, Po Luhuo and Shengguo supervised the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time there was another Po Luhuo. When Woshi pacified Shaanxi, Po Luhuo and Shengguo supervised the fighting.

sentences.zh: 後為平陽尹，西南路招討使，終於慶陽尹。

translations.literal: He later became prefect of Pingyang, southwestern-route pacification commissioner, and died as prefect of Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He later became prefect of Pingyang, southwestern-route pacification commissioner, and died as prefect of Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 泰州婆盧火守邊屢有功，太宗賜衣一襲，並賜其子剖叔。

translations.literal: Po Luhuo of Taizhou guarded the frontier with repeated merit; the Taizong granted him one suit of clothing and also granted his son Poushu.
translations.idiomatic: Po Luhuo of Taizhou guarded the frontier with repeated merit. The Taizong granted him one suit of clothing and also granted his son Poushu.

sentences.zh: 八年，以甲胄賜所部諸謀克。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, armor was granted to all the company commanders under his command.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, armor was granted to all the company commanders under his command.

sentences.zh: 天會十三年，加同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tianhui he was made Associate Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Tianhui he was made associate grand councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 天眷元年，駐烏骨迪烈地，薨。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjuan he was stationed at Wugudilie and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianjuan he was stationed at Wugudilie and died.

sentences.zh: 贈開府儀同三司，諡剛毅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Master of the Palace with the Honored Title of Opening the Government and Equal in Ceremony to the Three Excellencies, with the posthumous title Gangyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Grand Master of the Palace with the Honored Title of Opening the Government and Equal in Ceremony to the Three Excellencies, with the posthumous title Gangyi.

sentences.zh: 子剖叔，襲猛安，天眷二年，為泰州副都統，子斡帶，廣威將軍。

translations.literal: His son Poushu inherited the meng'an post; in the second year of Tianjuan he became deputy commander-in-chief of Taizhou. His son Wo Dai was made General of Expansive Might.
translations.idiomatic: His son Poushu inherited the meng'an post. In the second year of Tianjuan he became deputy commander-in-chief of Taizhou. His son Wo Dai was made General of Expansive Might.

sentences.zh: 吾紮忽

translations.literal: Wu Zahu
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zahu

sentences.zh: 婆速，官特進，子吾紮忽。

translations.literal: Basu, whose office was Special Advancement, had the son Wu Zahu.
translations.idiomatic: Basu, whose office was Special Advancement, had the son Wu Zahu.

sentences.zh: 吾紮忽，善騎射，年二十，以本班祗候郎君都管，從征伐有功，授修武校尉。

translations.literal: Wu Zahu was skilled in mounted archery. At twenty he served as chief steward of the attendant guards of the inner service and followed campaigns with merit, being appointed Colonel of Cultivated Martiality.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zahu was skilled in mounted archery. At twenty he served as chief steward of the attendant guards of the inner service and distinguished himself on campaign, being appointed Colonel of Cultivated Martiality.

sentences.zh: 皇統二年，權領泰州軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangtong he provisionally commanded the Taizhou army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Huangtong he provisionally commanded the Taizhou army.

sentences.zh: 平陝西，至涇州，大破宋兵于馬西鎮，超遷甯遠大將軍，襲猛安。

translations.literal: When Shaanxi was pacified, at Jingzhou he utterly defeated Song troops at Maxi Town, was promoted to General of Pacifying the Distance, and inherited the meng'an post.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaanxi was pacified, at Jingzhou he routed Song troops at Maxi Town, was promoted to General of Pacifying the Distance, and inherited the meng'an post.

sentences.zh: 複以本部軍從宗弼，權都統。

translations.literal: Again with his command he followed Zongbi as acting commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Again with his command he followed Zongbi as acting commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 正隆末，從海陵伐宋。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhenlong reign he followed Hailing in the campaign against Song.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhenlong reign he followed Hailing in the campaign against Song.

sentences.zh: 契丹反，與德昌軍節度使移至懣同討契丹，許以便宜從事。

translations.literal: When the Khitan rebelled, he joined Dechang Army military commissioner Yizhiman in suppressing the Khitan, with authority to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan rebelled, he joined Dechang Army military commissioner Yizhiman in suppressing the Khitan, with authority to act as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 大定初，除咸平尹，駐軍泰州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dading he was made prefect of Xianping and encamped the army at Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Dading he was made prefect of Xianping and encamped the army at Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 俄改臨潢尹，攝元帥左都監。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to prefect of Linhuang and acted as left marshal supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was changed to prefect of Linhuang and acted as left marshal supervisor.

sentences.zh: 與廣甯尹僕散渾坦俱從元帥右都監神土懣解臨潢之圍。

translations.literal: Together with Guangning prefect Pusan Huntan he followed the right marshal supervisor Shentuman in relieving the siege of Linhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Guangning prefect Pusan Huntan he followed the right marshal supervisor Shentuman in relieving the siege of Linhuang.

sentences.zh: 契丹引眾東行，吾紮忽追及於窊曆山。

translations.literal: The Khitan led their host east; Wu Zahu overtook them at Walishan.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan led their host east. Wu Zahu overtook them at Walishan.

sentences.zh: 押軍猛安契丹忽刺叔以所部助敵，攻官軍，官軍失利。

translations.literal: Escort-army meng'an, the Khitan Hulaci, aided the enemy with his command, attacked the government army, and the government army suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Escort-army meng'an, the Khitan Hulaci, aided the enemy with his command, attacked the government army, and the government army was defeated.

sentences.zh: 泰州節度使烏裏雅來救，未至臨潢與敵遇，烏裏雅敗，僅以數騎脫歸。

translations.literal: Taizhou military commissioner Wuliya came to rescue them; before reaching Linhuang he met the enemy, Wuliya was defeated, and escaped with only a few horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Taizhou military commissioner Wuliya came to rescue them. Before reaching Linhuang he met the enemy; Wuliya was defeated and escaped with only a few horsemen.

sentences.zh: 敵攻泰州，其勢大振，城中震駭，將士不敢出戰，敵四面登城。

translations.literal: The enemy attacked Taizhou; their momentum grew greatly, the city was shaken with terror, officers and soldiers dared not go out to fight, and the enemy climbed the walls on all four sides.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy attacked Taizhou. Their momentum grew greatly, the city was shaken with terror, officers and soldiers dared not go out to fight, and the enemy climbed the walls on all four sides.

sentences.zh: 押軍猛安烏古孫阿裏補率軍士數人持钅算刀循城，應敵力戰，斫刈甚眾，敵乃退，泰州得完。

translations.literal: Escort-army meng'an Wugusun Alibu led several soldiers with pole blades along the wall, met the enemy and fought fiercely, cutting down many; the enemy then withdrew and Taizhou was preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: Escort-army meng'an Wugusun Alibu led several soldiers with pole blades along the wall, met the enemy and fought fiercely, cutting down many. The enemy then withdrew and Taizhou was preserved intact.

sentences.zh: 吾紮忽乃使謀克蒲盧渾徙百姓旁邑及險厄之地，以俟大軍。

translations.literal: Wu Zahu then had company commander Puluhun move the people to neighboring towns and defensible places to await the main army.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zahu then had company commander Puluhun move the people to neighboring towns and defensible places to await the main army.

sentences.zh: 明年，聚甲士萬三千於濟州，會元帥謀衍，敗窩斡於長濼。

translations.literal: The next year thirteen thousand armored soldiers were gathered at Jizhou; they joined Marshal Moyan and defeated Wowo at Changchi.
translations.idiomatic: The next year thirteen thousand armored soldiers were gathered at Jizhou. They joined Marshal Moyan and defeated Wowo at Changchi.

sentences.zh: 戰霿{箣松}河，戰陷泉，皆有功，改胡裏改節度使，卒。

translations.literal: They fought at the Mengsong River and at Xianquan, all with merit; he was made military commissioner of Huligai and died.
translations.idiomatic: They fought at the Mengsong River and at Xianquan, distinguishing themselves in both. He was made military commissioner of Huligai and died.

sentences.zh: 吾紮忽性聰敏，有才智，善用軍，常出敵之不意，故能以寡敵眾，而所往無不克，號為「鶻軍」雲。

translations.literal: Wu Zahu was clever and quick-witted, possessed talent and wisdom, and skilled in using troops; he often struck where the enemy did not expect, and so could use few against many; wherever he went he did not fail to conquer, and he was called the "Hawk Army."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zahu was clever and quick-witted, possessed talent and wisdom, and skilled in using troops. He often struck where the enemy did not expect, and so could use few against many. Wherever he went he did not fail to conquer, and he was called the "Hawk Army."

sentences.zh: 闍母，世祖第十一子，太祖異母弟也。

translations.literal: She Mu was the eleventh son of the founding Ancestor and the Taizu's younger half-brother.
translations.idiomatic: She Mu was the eleventh son of the founding Ancestor and the Taizu's younger half-brother.

sentences.zh: 高永昌據東京，斡魯往伐之，闍母等為之佐。

translations.literal: When Gao Yongchang seized the Eastern Capital, Wo Lu went to attack him and She Mu and others assisted him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Yongchang seized the Eastern Capital, Wo Lu went to attack him, and She Mu and others assisted.

sentences.zh: 已克瀋州，城中出奔者闍母邀擊殆盡。

translations.literal: After Shenzhou had been taken, those who fled from the city were intercepted and nearly all destroyed by She Mu.
translations.idiomatic: After Shenzhou was taken, those who fled from the city were intercepted and nearly all destroyed by She Mu.

sentences.zh: 與永昌隔沃裏活水，眾遇淖不敢進，闍母以所部先濟，諸軍畢濟。

translations.literal: Separated from Yongchang by the Wolihuo River, the host encountered marsh and dared not advance; She Mu crossed first with his command, and all the armies then crossed.
translations.idiomatic: Separated from Yongchang by the Wolihuo River, the host encountered marsh and dared not advance. She Mu crossed first with his command, and all the armies then crossed.

sentences.zh: 軍東京城下，城中人出城來戰，闍母破之於首山，殲其眾，獲馬五百匹。

translations.literal: The army reached below the Eastern Capital walls; the people came out to fight and She Mu defeated them at Shoushan, annihilating their host and capturing five hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: The army reached below the Eastern Capital walls. The people came out to fight, and She Mu defeated them at Shoushan, annihilating their host and capturing five hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 及斡魯古以罪去鹹州，闍母氏代之，於是闍母為咸州路副統。

translations.literal: When Wolugu was removed from Xianzhou because of his crimes, She Mu's clan replaced him; She Mu thus became deputy commander of the Xianzhou Route.
translations.idiomatic: When Wolugu was removed from Xianzhou because of his crimes, She Mu's clan replaced him, and She Mu became deputy commander of the Xianzhou Route.

sentences.zh: 遼議和久不成，太祖進兵，詔咸州路都統司，令斜葛留兵一千鎮守，闍母以余兵會於渾河。

translations.literal: Peace talks with Liao dragged on without success; the Taizu advanced his armies. He ordered the Xianzhou Route commander-in-chief's office to leave Xiege with a thousand troops to garrison the place, and She Mu joined the remainder at the Hun River.
translations.idiomatic: Peace talks with the Liao dragged on without success, and the Taizu advanced his armies. He ordered the Xianzhou Route commander-in-chief's office to leave Xiege with a thousand troops to garrison the place, and She Mu joined the remainder at the Hun River.

sentences.zh: 太祖攻上京，實臨潢府，諭之不下。

translations.literal: The Taizu attacked the Upper Capital, which was in fact Linhuang Prefecture, but could not take it by persuasion.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu attacked the Upper Capital, which was in fact Linhuang Prefecture, but could not take it by persuasion.

sentences.zh: 遼人恃儲蓄自固。

translations.literal: The Liao relied on their stores and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao relied on their stores and held firm.

sentences.zh: 上親臨陣，闍母以眾先登，克其外城，留守撻不野率眾出降。

translations.literal: The emperor came personally to the battle line; She Mu led his host up first and took the outer city; the defending commander Tabuye led his host out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came personally to the battle line. She Mu led his host up first and took the outer city. The defending commander Tabuye led his host out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 都統杲兵至中京，闍母自城西沿土河以進，城中兵尚餘三千，皆不能守，遂克之。

translations.literal: Commander-in-chief Gao's troops reached Central Capital; She Mu advanced along the Tuhu River from the west of the city. More than three thousand troops remained in the city yet could not hold it, and it was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Commander-in-chief Gao's troops reached Central Capital. She Mu advanced along the Tuhu River from the west of the city. More than three thousand troops remained in the city yet could not hold it, and it was taken.

sentences.zh: 宗翰等攻西京，闍母、婁室等於城東為木洞以捍蔽矢石，於北隅以芻茭塞其隍，城中出兵萬餘，將燒之。

translations.literal: When Zonghan and the others attacked the Western Capital, She Mu, Woshi, and the others built wooden tunnels on the east of the city to shield against arrows and stones, and at the north corner stuffed the moat with straw; more than ten thousand men came out of the city intending to burn them.
translations.idiomatic: When Zonghan and the others attacked the Western Capital, She Mu, Woshi, and the others built wooden tunnels on the east of the city to shield against arrows and stones, and at the north corner stuffed the moat with straw. More than ten thousand men came out of the city intending to burn them.

sentences.zh: 溫蒂罕蒲匣率眾力戰，執旗者被創，蒲匣自執旗，奮擊卻之。

translations.literal: Wendihan Puxia led the host and fought fiercely; the banner-bearer was wounded, Puxia himself took the banner, struck fiercely, and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: Wendihan Puxia led the host and fought fiercely. The banner-bearer was wounded; Puxia himself took the banner, struck fiercely, and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 又為四輪革車，高出於堞，闍母與麾下乘車先登，諸軍繼之，遂克西京。

translations.literal: They also made four-wheeled leather wagons higher than the parapets; She Mu and his followers mounted the wagons and went up first, the armies followed, and the Western Capital was taken.
translations.idiomatic: They also made four-wheeled leather wagons higher than the parapets. She Mu and his followers mounted the wagons and went up first; the armies followed, and the Western Capital was taken.

sentences.zh: 與遼步騎五千戰於朔州之境，，斬首三百級。

translations.literal: They fought five thousand Liao infantry and cavalry in the region of Shuozhou and beheaded three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: They fought five thousand Liao infantry and cavalry in the region of Shuozhou and beheaded three hundred.

sentences.zh: 複敗遼騎三百于河陰。

translations.literal: They again defeated three hundred Liao horsemen south of the river.
translations.idiomatic: They again defeated three hundred Liao horsemen south of the river.

sentences.zh: 遼兵五千屯于馬邑縣南，複擊破之，隳其營壘，盡得其車馬、器械。

translations.literal: Five thousand Liao troops were encamped south of Mayi County; they were again struck and defeated, their camps destroyed, and all their carts, horses, and weapons were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Five thousand Liao troops were encamped south of Mayi County. They were again struck and defeated, their camps destroyed, and all their carts, horses, and weapons were taken.

sentences.zh: 遼兵三萬，列營於西京之西，闍母以三千擊之。

translations.literal: Thirty thousand Liao troops encamped west of the Western Capital; She Mu attacked them with three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty thousand Liao troops encamped west of the Western Capital. She Mu attacked them with three thousand.

sentences.zh: 闍母使士卒皆去馬，陣於溝塹之間，曰：「以一擊十，不致之死地，不可使戰也。」

translations.literal: She Mu had the soldiers all dismount and form battle lines in the ditches and ramparts, saying: "With one against ten, if we do not fight to the death we cannot make battle."
translations.idiomatic: She Mu had the soldiers dismount and form battle lines in the ditches and ramparts, saying, "One against ten — if we do not fight to the death we cannot make battle."

sentences.zh: 謂眾曰：「若不勝敵，不可以求生。」

translations.literal: He told the host: "If we do not defeat the enemy, we cannot hope to live."
translations.idiomatic: He told the host, "If we do not defeat the enemy, we cannot hope to live."

sentences.zh: 於是人皆殊死戰，遼兵遂敗，追至其營而止。

translations.literal: Thereupon every man fought as if certain to die; the Liao army was defeated and pursuit continued to their camp before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon every man fought as if certain to die. The Liao army was defeated and pursuit continued to their camp before stopping.

sentences.zh: 明日，複敗其兵七百餘人。

translations.literal: The next day they again defeated more than seven hundred of their troops.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they again defeated more than seven hundred of their troops.

sentences.zh: 興中府宜州複叛，闍母討之，並下詔招諭，詔闍母曰：「遼之土地皆為我有，彼雖複叛，終皆吾民，可縱其耕稼，毋得侵掠。」

translations.literal: Xingzhong Prefecture's Yizhou rebelled again; She Mu suppressed them and also issued an edict to summon and instruct them. The edict to She Mu said: "All Liao lands are now mine; though they rebel again, in the end they are all my people. Let them plow and sow — do not raid or plunder."
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou in Xingzhong Prefecture rebelled again. She Mu suppressed them and also issued an edict to summon and instruct the people. The edict to She Mu said, "All Liao lands are now mine. Though they rebel again, in the end they are all my people. Let them plow and sow — do not raid or plunder."

sentences.zh: 勃堇蒙刮、斜缽、吾撻等獲契丹九斤，興中平。

translations.literal: The lords Menggua, Xiebo, and Wuta captured the Khitan Jiujin, and Xingzhong was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The lords Menggua, Xiebo, and Wuta captured the Khitan Jiujin, and Xingzhong was pacified.

sentences.zh: 闍母為南路都統，討回離保，詔曰：「回離保以烏合之眾，保據險阻，其勢必將自斃。

translations.literal: She Mu became southern-route commander-in-chief and campaigned against Huilibao. The edict said: "Huilibao, with a mob gathered from all sides, holds rugged defiles — his force will surely destroy itself.
translations.idiomatic: She Mu became southern-route commander-in-chief and campaigned against Huilibao. The edict said, "Huilibao, with a mob gathered from all sides, holds rugged defiles — his force will surely destroy itself.

sentences.zh: 若彼不出掠，毋庸攻討。」

translations.literal: If they do not come out to raid, there is no need to attack."
translations.idiomatic: If they do not come out to raid, there is no need to attack."

sentences.zh: 耶律奧古哲等殺回離保于景、薊之間，其眾遂潰。

translations.literal: Yelü Aoguzhe and others killed Huilibao between Jing and Ji; his host then scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Aoguzhe and others killed Huilibao between Jing and Ji, and his host scattered.

sentences.zh: 張覺據平州叛，入于宋，闍母自錦州往討之。

translations.literal: Zhang Jue held Pingzhou and rebelled, entering Song service; She Mu went from Jinzhou to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jue held Pingzhou and rebelled, entering Song service. She Mu went from Jinzhou to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 覺將以兵脅遷、來、潤、隰四州之民闍母至潤州，擊走張覺軍，逐北至榆關，遣俘侍書招之。

translations.literal: Jue intended to coerce the people of Qian, Lai, Run, and Xi prefectures. When She Mu reached Runzhou he struck and drove off Zhang Jue's army, pursued north to Yuguan, and sent captives with a letter of instruction to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Jue intended to coerce the people of Qian, Lai, Run, and Xi prefectures. When She Mu reached Runzhou he struck and drove off Zhang Jue's army, pursued north to Yuguan, and sent captives with a letter of instruction to summon him.

sentences.zh: 複敗覺兵于營州東北，欲乘勝進取南京。

translations.literal: He again defeated Jue's army northeast of Yingzhou and wished to press the victory to take the Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He again defeated Jue's army northeast of Yingzhou and wished to press the victory to take the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 時方暑雨，退屯海鹆需，逐水草休息，使僕虺、蒙刮兩猛安屯潤州，制未降州縣，不得與覺交通。

translations.literal: It was then the season of summer rains; they withdrew and encamped at Haiyu, following water and grass to rest, leaving the meng'an Pu Hui and Menggua to garrison Runzhou, controlling the unsubmitted prefectures and counties and forbidding contact with Jue.
translations.idiomatic: It was then the season of summer rains. They withdrew and encamped at Haiyu, following water and grass to rest, leaving the meng'an Pu Hui and Menggua to garrison Runzhou, controlling the unsubmitted prefectures and counties and forbidding contact with Jue.

sentences.zh: 九月，闍母破覺將王孝古於新安，敗覺軍于樓峰口。

translations.literal: In the ninth month She Mu defeated Jue's general Wang Xiaogu at Xin'an and defeated Jue's army at Loufengkou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month She Mu defeated Jue's general Wang Xiaogu at Xin'an and defeated Jue's army at Loufengkou.

sentences.zh: 複與覺戰於兔耳山，闍母大敗。

translations.literal: He again fought Jue at Tuer Mountain and She Mu suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He again fought Jue at Tuer Mountain and She Mu suffered a great defeat.

sentences.zh: 太宗使宗望問闍母敗軍之狀，宗望遂以闍母軍討覺。

translations.literal: The Taizong sent Zongwang to inquire into the circumstances of She Mu's defeated army; Zongwang then used She Mu's army to campaign against Jue.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizong sent Zongwang to inquire into the circumstances of She Mu's defeated army. Zongwang then used She Mu's army to campaign against Jue.

sentences.zh: 及宗望破張覺，太宗乃赦闍母，召宗望赴闕。

translations.literal: When Zongwang defeated Zhang Jue, the Taizong then pardoned She Mu and summoned Zongwang to court.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongwang defeated Zhang Jue, the Taizong pardoned She Mu and summoned Zongwang to court.

sentences.zh: 闍母連破偽都統張敦固，遂克南京，執敦固殺之。

translations.literal: She Mu repeatedly defeated the acting commander-in-chief Zhang Dungu and then took the Southern Capital, seized Dungu, and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: She Mu repeatedly defeated the acting commander-in-chief Zhang Dungu, then took the Southern Capital, seized Dungu, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 上遣使迎勞之，詔曰：「聞下南京，撫定兵民，甚善。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys to welcome and reward him. The edict said: "I hear you have descended on the Southern Capital and pacified troops and people — very good.
